item.research_question: Can independently controllable multiple coherent precipitation structures be tailored by stepwise thermo-mechanical processes to generate ultrahigh strength and ductile refractory high-entropy alloys?
item.material_system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (at.%) refractory high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase bcc/fcc structure
item.processing_route: Arc melting followed by homogenization at 1200 °C for 5 h, hot rolling at 1200 °C (80% reduction), cold rolling at 25 °C (75% reduction), annealing at 900 °C for 5 min, and aging at 650 °C for 20 h followed by water quenching
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature (strain rate 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹) and elevated temperatures up to 800 °C (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); microstructural characterization via EBSD, TEM, STEM, and APT
key_findings: The alloy achieved an ultrahigh ultimate tensile strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature.
The yield strength of the as-cast structure was ~600 MPa, increasing to ~1.4 GPa after Step I (δ-lamella precipitation) and further to 2.0 GPa after Step II (γ″-particle precipitation).
The alloy retained a high yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C due to the stability of the grain structure and precipitates.
The δ-lamellae have a width of ~40 nm and length of 0.5 to 1 μm, while the γ″ particles are spheroidal with a size of ~10 nm.
Both δ (D0a structure) and γ″ (D022 structure) precipitates share a similar composition of (Ni 70 Fe 5) 3 (Ta 20 W 5).
The coherent interfaces of the precipitates allowed dislocations to shear the δ-lamellae and be pinned by γ″ particles without causing premature crack initiation.
The SCCPs structure remained stable after annealing at 800 °C for 50 h (δ phase) and 40 h (γ″ particles).
The strain-hardening rate remained high even at high stress levels, contributing to the enhanced ductility.
item.mechanism: The coherent interfaces of the stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation. The δ-lamellae hinder dislocation motion via lamellar boundaries and are sheared by slip bands, leading to coherent misalignment rather than cracking. The γ″ particles provide order hardening and lattice misfit strengthening while their small size and low lattice misfit prevent crack initiation at the precipitate-matrix interface. The synergistic effect of these two coherent precipitates provides ~1 GPa of strength while maintaining ductility.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that traditional single-principal-element systems and other refractory HEAs suffer from brittle phases or limited ductility.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the SCCPs design concept may afford a means to develop a wide range of ultrahigh-strength metallic materials by providing a pathway for alloy design.
